summary: Source decomposition of the analytic and algebraic core of the roadmap from two primary sources read directly: Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams Sec. 3 (read in full, printed pp. 13-26) and Sec. 13.1 plus Appendix A.1 (printed pp. 65-66, 73-77), and Colmez, Fonctions d'une variable p-adique, Asterisque 330, Secs. I.1, I.2, II.2 and II.4 (printed pp. 14-20, 41-42, 46-47). Stages L0, L1, L2 and L3 are decomposed from proofs actually read; L3 is the only stage whose whole stated scope and imports are accounted for. Two structural points are recorded against the sources. (1) RJW Lemma 3.38's proof opens 'As p is odd, (Z_p/p^n)^x is cyclic', so the principal augmentation-ideal theorem, and with it the shape mu/([a]-[1]) of every pseudo-measure and the weight-space simple-pole description, carries an odd-p hypothesis that must not be dropped at p = 2. (2) RJW Remark 3.35 asserts that integration against a nontrivial character 'induces a unique homomorphism Q(G) -> C_p'; that is too strong, since a denominator in the total quotient ring can have zero chi-integral. Formula (3.11) is unaffected because its denominators are chosen with chi(g) - 1 nonzero, but the homomorphism exists only on the localization at the elements with nonvanishing chi-integral. Mahler's theorem, which RJW imports as [Col10a, Thm. I.2.3], has been read in Colmez with its full proof, so that import is closed rather than packaged. The structure theorem for Lambda-modules, Weierstrass division, Coates-Sujatha's Appendix A.1, and Amice's rigid description of weight space are all quoted-not-proved in the available sources and are recorded as explicit gaps with their next source actions; Washington, Coates-Sujatha, NSW and BGR are absent from the supplied library. Stage L6 was not opened.

nodes.title: Existence and recognition of orthonormal bases of an L-Banach space
nodes.statement: Let L be a discretely valued complete subfield of C_p with uniformizer pi_L, and let B be an L-Banach space with valuation v_B. Then (i) B admits a Banach basis; (ii) B admits an orthonormal basis if and only if v_B(B) = v_p(L), and in that case, writing B^0 = {x in B : v_B(x) >= 0} and Bbar = B^0/pi_L B^0, a family (e_i)_{i in I} of elements of B^0 is an orthonormal basis of B if and only if the reductions (ebar_i) form an algebraic basis of the k_L-vector space Bbar.
hypotheses: L is a complete subfield of C_p with discrete valuation and uniformizer pi_L; v_p is normalized by v_p(p)=1
B is complete for the valuation v_B (an L-Banach space in the sense of Colmez Sec. I.1.1)
For part (ii) the value group condition v_B(B) = v_p(L) is required; without it only Banach (non-isometric) bases are obtained
'Orthonormal basis' means the map (a_i) -> sum a_i e_i from c_0(I,L) to B is an isometry, not merely an isomorphism
proofSteps: Replace v_B by the equivalent valuation v'_B(x) = v_p(pi_L) * ceil(v_B(x)/v_p(pi_L)), which takes values in v_p(L); this deduces (i) from (ii).

Given (e_i) in B^0 whose reductions form a k_L-basis of Bbar, fix a set-theoretic section s : k_L -> O_L of reduction with s(0)=0 and extend it to B^0 by s(x) = sum_i s(a_i) e_i for x = sum a_i ebar_i; then x - s(x) lies in pi_L B^0.
Iterate: x_0 = x, x_{n+1} = pi_L^{-1}(x_n - s(x_n)); then x = sum_{n<=k} pi_L^n s(x_n) + pi_L^{k+1} x_{k+1}, so setting a_i = sum_n pi_L^n s_{n,i} gives a surjection c_0(I,L) -> B.
If v_{c_0}(a) = 0 then sum a_i e_i is nonzero mod pi_L because the ebar_i are a basis; combined with v_B(B) = v_p(pi_L) Z this forces v_B(sum a_i e_i) = 0, so the map is an isometry.

Conversely, from an orthonormal basis lift x in Bbar to x in B^0, expand x = sum a_i e_i with a_i -> 0, and observe abar_i is nonzero only for the finitely many i with v_p(a_i)=0; linear independence follows from v_B(x) = inf_i v_p(a_i).
acceptance: Instantiate with B = C(Z_p,L) and e_n = binom(x,n): Colmez Cor. I.2.4 recovers Mahler's orthonormal basis, so the criterion must reproduce it
Exhibit an L-Banach space with v_B(B) strictly larger than v_p(L) (e.g. a one-dimensional space rescaled by an element of C_p outside L) and check only a Banach basis is produced
Check the conclusion is an isometry, not merely a topological isomorphism

sources.match: The successive-expansion recursion named in the stage text ('lifting a basis of the integral lattice modulo varpi and completing the successive expansions') is exactly this construction.

sources.excerpt: By [Col10a, Prop. I.1.5], if B is an L-Banach space with valuation v_B, and v_B(B) = v_p(L), then B admits an orthonormal basis.
sources.match: Fixes which direction of Colmez's proposition the roadmap's normative source actually uses.

nodes.title: The two topologies on the continuous dual of an L-Banach space
nodes.statement: For an L-Banach space B, the continuous dual B* = Hom_cts(B,L) carries (a) the strong topology defined by v*(mu) = inf_{x in B} (v_p(mu(x)) - v_B(x)), for which B* is an L-Banach space, and (b) the weak topology of pointwise convergence, defined by the semivaluations v_x(mu) = v_p(mu(x)). B* is complete for both; it is an L-Banach space for the weak topology only when B is finite dimensional. B is reflexive only when B* carries the weak topology.
hypotheses: B is an L-Banach space; L complete, v_p(p)=1
Weak completeness is deduced from Banach-Steinhaus for L-Banach spaces (Colmez Prop. I.1.2(ii)), so it is a theorem about duals of Banach spaces, not an arbitrary topological vector space statement
v_x is a semivaluation: it satisfies the ultrametric and homogeneity axioms but not v(x)=+infinity => x=0
proofSteps: Define v* and check it is a valuation on B*; completeness for v* is the usual uniform-limit argument on the unit ball.
For the weak topology, a pointwise limit of continuous linear maps on an L-Banach space is continuous by Banach-Steinhaus (Colmez Prop. I.1.2(ii)); hence B* is weakly complete.
Observe the weak topology is not normable unless dim B < infinity, so 'weakly complete' does not mean 'weakly Banach'.
acceptance: Under the Amice transform of L2, check the strong topology corresponds to the p-adic topology on O_L[[T]] and the weak topology to the (p,T)-adic topology (RJW Remark 3.28(3))
Verify the sequence 1, T, T^2, ... converges to 0 weakly but not strongly

sources.excerpt: D'apres le theoreme de Banach-Steinhaus, B* est aussi complet pour la topologie faible, mais l'espace ainsi obtenu n'est un L-banach que si B est de dimension finie.
sources.match: Gives both the weak completeness assertion and the exact reason it does not make B* a Banach space; the stage text had left weak completeness unasserted.

sources.locator: Sec. 3.1, Def. 3.5 and Remark 3.6, printed p. 14
sources.excerpt: The dual B* is complete with both of these topologies. However generally it is an L-Banach space only for the strong topology, whilst B is reflexive (canonically isomorphic to its double continuous dual) only when B* is equipped with the weak topology.
sources.match: Confirms the same statement in the roadmap's normative reference and adds the reflexivity clause the stage needs.

nodes.title: Bounded measures on a profinite space and their integral lattice
nodes.statement: For a profinite abelian group G (or any closed subset X of one, with the subspace topology) let C(G,L) be the L-Banach space of continuous functions with v_C(phi) = inf_{x in G} v_p(phi(x)). Define M(G,L) = C(G,L)* = Hom_cts(C(G,L),L). A measure mu lies in the integral lattice M(G,O_L) if and only if the integral of every O_L-valued continuous function against mu lies in O_L; then M(G,L) = M(G,O_L) tensor_{O_L} L, i.e. every bounded measure is a scalar multiple of an integral one.
hypotheses: G compact (profinite), so every continuous phi : G -> L is bounded and v_C is well defined
Continuity of a linear functional on C(G,L) is equivalent to boundedness; this is what makes the integral-lattice scaling statement true
The definition is stated for a compact X; a noncompact X requires a separately specified function space and is not covered
proofSteps: v_C is a valuation on C(G,L) because G is compact; completeness makes C(G,L) an L-Banach space.
Define M(G,O_L) as the subset of M(G,L) mapping C(G,O_L) into O_L; this is an O_L-submodule.
Given a continuous mu, its operator valuation v*(mu) is finite, so p^{-v*(mu)} rounded to an element of L scales mu into M(G,O_L); this gives M(G,L) = M(G,O_L)[1/p].
acceptance: Check Dirac measures delta_g lie in M(G,O_L)
Check that the real-valued Haar measure of Z_p (with measure p^{-n} on a+p^n Z_p) is not a p-adic measure because it is unbounded
Check the identity M(G,L) = M(G,O_L) tensor L fails if boundedness is dropped

sources.locator: Sec. 3.2, Defs. 3.7-3.8 and Remark 3.9, printed pp. 14-15
sources.excerpt: We say that an element mu in M(G,L) is an O_L-valued measure, and write mu in M(G,O_L), if the integral of phi against mu lies in O_L for every O_L-valued function phi. Since measures are continuous (or equivalently, bounded), we have M(G,L) = M(G,O_L) tensor_{O_L} L.
sources.match: Exactly the integral-lattice description and the scaling statement the stage requires, with the boundedness equivalence made explicit.

sources.excerpt: On Z_p, we have a (real-valued) Haar measure defined so that open compact subsets of the form a+p^n Z_p have measure p^{-n}. Whilst this is probably the most natural measure one might consider on Z_p, observe that this is not a p-adic measure, as it is not p-adically bounded!
sources.match: Supplies the acceptance counterexample distinguishing bounded from arbitrary finitely additive functions.

nodes.title: Density of locally constant functions and the finitely additive description of measures
nodes.statement: Restriction along C^{lc}(G,O_L) contained in C(G,O_L) is an isomorphism M(G,O_L) -> M^{lc}(G,O_L) = Hom_cts(C^{lc}(G,O_L),O_L), and M^{lc}(G,O_L) is identified with the O_L-module of finitely additive functions mu from the set of compact open subsets of G to O_L, via mu(U) = integral of 1_U. Consequently M(G,O_L) is the module of finitely additive O_L-valued functions on compact opens, and M(G,L) is the module of *bounded* finitely additive L-valued functions.
hypotheses: G profinite: the compact open subgroups form a neighbourhood basis of the identity, so every locally constant function factors through a finite quotient G/H
The inverse construction requires the limit of the integrals of an approximating sequence to be independent of the approximating sequence; this uses continuity of mu^{lc}
The unbounded case is excluded: an arbitrary finitely additive L-valued function need not be a measure
proofSteps: Density: RJW writes the truncations phi_n = sum_{a in Z/p^n} phi(a) 1_{a+p^n Z_p}, which is the argument for G = Z_p; for a general profinite G the same argument runs with the finite clopen partition of G by cosets of an open subgroup H, using uniform continuity on the compact G.
Given mu^{lc}, define the integral of a continuous phi as the limit of the integrals of the phi_n; continuity makes the limit exist and be independent of the choice, giving the inverse map.

For the finitely additive description, set mu(U) = integral of 1_U; conversely, for phi locally constant factoring through G/H, define the integral as sum over cosets aH of phi(a) mu(aH). Additivity of mu makes this independent of H.
acceptance: Check the two descriptions agree on Dirac measures: delta_g corresponds to the indicator function X -> 1 if g in X, 0 otherwise
Verify the density argument on a profinite group with no Z_p-like coordinate, e.g. an infinite product of finite groups, using clopen cosets rather than residue classes
Check that dropping boundedness breaks the L-valued statement

sources.excerpt: Let C^{lc}(G,O_L) denote the space of locally constant functions G -> O_L; this is a dense subspace of the continuous functions C(G,O_L).
sources.match: States the density used for the extension-from-dense-test-functions requirement of the stage.

sources.excerpt: Indeed, any continuous function phi in C(G,O_L) can be p-adically approximated by its locally constant truncations phi_n(x) = sum_{a in (Z/p^n Z)} phi(a) 1_{a+p^n Z_p}(x).
sources.match: This is the passage the stage description flags: RJW's written approximation uses residue classes of Z_p even though the ambient statement is for a general profinite G, so the general case has to be run with clopen cosets of an open subgroup.

sources.excerpt: We have an identification of M^{lc}(G,O_L) with the space of additive functions mu : {open compact subsets of G} -> O_L.
sources.match: The finitely additive description the stage asks to establish, in the integral case.

nodes.title: The continuous dual of c_0(I,L) is ell-infinity(I,L), isometrically
nodes.statement: For any index set I, the pairing (b,a) -> sum_{i in I} b_i a_i converges for b in ell-infinity(I,L) and a in c_0(I,L), and b -> f_b is an isometry of ell-infinity(I,L) onto the continuous dual of c_0(I,L). Moreover every f in the dual is the weak (not strong, unless I is finite) sum of the series sum_i f(delta_i) delta_i^*.
hypotheses: L complete; c_0(I,L) is the space of families tending to 0 along the filter of complements of finite sets, with v(a) = inf_i v_p(a_i)
Surjectivity uses continuity of f and density of the span of the delta_i in c_0(I,L)
The last clause holds only for the weak topology on the dual when I is infinite
proofSteps: Convergence of the series follows from v_p(b_i a_i) >= v_{ell-infinity}(b) + v_p(a_i) and a_i -> 0.
Given f in the dual, set b_i = f(delta_i); continuity gives v_p(b_i) >= v*(f), so b lies in ell-infinity(I,L).
f - f_b vanishes on the span of the delta_i, which is dense; by continuity f = f_b.
Isometry follows by computing v* on both sides.
acceptance: Combine with the Mahler basis of L2 to recover that a measure on Z_p is exactly a bounded sequence of Mahler moments
Check the failure of strong convergence of sum_i f(delta_i) delta_i^* when I is infinite

sources.locator: Sec. I.1.3, Prop. I.1.6 and Remark I.1.7, printed p. 17
sources.excerpt: Si f_b(a) designe la somme de la serie sum_i b_i a_i, l'application b -> f_b est une isometrie de ell-infinity(I,L) sur le dual de c_0(I,L).
sources.match: This is the abstract statement behind 'a bounded measure is exactly a bounded family of moments' used by the Mahler/Amice identification of stage L2, and it is the source of the boundedness (as opposed to merely finite-additivity) condition.

nodes.title: Completed tensor products and base change of orthonormal bases
nodes.statement: For L-Banach spaces B_1, B_2 the completed tensor product B_1 hat-tensor_L B_2 is the separated completion of B_1 tensor_L B_2 for the semivaluation v(z) = max over representations z = sum_j x_j tensor y_j of inf_j (v_{B_1}(x_j)+v_{B_2}(y_j)); then c_0(I,L) hat-tensor_L B is isometric to c_0(I,B). Consequently, if (e_i) and (f_j) are orthonormal bases of B_1 and B_2 then (e_i tensor f_j) is an orthonormal basis of B_1 hat-tensor_L B_2; and if K is a complete subfield of C_p containing L, an orthonormal basis of B is an orthonormal basis of the K-Banach space K hat-tensor_L B.
hypotheses: Both factors are L-Banach spaces; the semivaluation is the maximum over all representations, not a fixed one
The base-change statement is for a complete extension K of L inside C_p
proofSteps: Prove c_0(I,L) hat-tensor_L B is isometric to c_0(I,B) by comparing the two valuations in both directions; the nontrivial direction expands each tensor factor in a finite basis of the span of the y_j and splits off a finite index set I_0.
Deduce the orthonormal-basis statements as corollaries.
acceptance: Check that the scalar extension in the roots-of-unity formulas of L2 (which adjoin mu_{p^n} to L) preserves the Mahler orthonormal basis and hence preserves integrality statements
Check the completed tensor of two Iwasawa algebras against the Iwasawa algebra of the product group

sources.locator: Sec. I.1.4, Prop. I.1.8 and Cor. I.1.9, printed pp. 17-18
sources.excerpt: Corollaire 1.1.9. - (i) Si B_1 et B_2 sont des L-banach et si (e_i) et (f_j) sont des bases orthonormales de B_1 et B_2, alors (e_i tensor f_j) est une base orthonormale de B_1 hat-tensor_L B_2. (ii) Si B est un L-banach, si (e_i) est une base orthonormale de B, et si K est un sous-corps complet de C_p contenant L, alors (e_i) est une base orthonormale du K-banach K hat-tensor_L B.
sources.match: Supplies the 'continuous scalar extension along isometric embeddings of p-adic fields' and 'completed tensor products when needed' items of stage L0 with their exact hypotheses.

nodes.title: The C_p-points of weight space for Z_p^x and the rigid description of measures
nodes.statement: For p odd, W(C_p) = Hom_cts(Z_p^x, C_p^x) decomposes as the disjoint union over the p-1 characters nu of mu_{p-1} of subsets U_nu = {chi : chi restricted to mu_{p-1} equals nu}, each identified with the open unit ball B(0,1) by evaluating at a fixed topological generator of 1+pZ_p. Under Amice's theorem a measure mu on Z_p^x is the same as a bounded rigid analytic function F_mu on W, with F_mu(chi) = the integral of chi against mu, multiplicative convolution corresponding to pointwise multiplication; a pseudo-measure corresponds to a rigid function with at worst a simple pole at the trivial character.
hypotheses: p odd: the decomposition Z_p^x = mu_{p-1} x (1+pZ_p) is used. At p=2 the corresponding decomposition is {+-1} x (1+4Z_2) and the count of components changes, so the p-1 discs statement does not apply
Evaluation at a topological generator of 1+pZ_p identifies Hom_cts(1+pZ_p, C_p^x) with B(0,1); this depends on the chosen generator
'Bounded' is essential: unbounded rigid functions correspond to distributions, not measures

The simple-pole statement uses the shape mu/([a]-[1]) of a pseudo-measure from stage L3 and the fact that the integral of chi against [a]-[1] vanishes exactly at chi trivial, because a is a topological generator
proofSteps: Split Hom_cts(Z_p^x, C_p^x) using Z_p^x = mu_{p-1} x (1+pZ_p).
Identify the second factor with B(0,1) by chi -> chi(gamma)-1 for gamma a topological generator.
Invoke Amice's theorem to identify bounded rigid functions on W with measures on Z_p^x; RJW states this without proof.
For a pseudo-measure lambda = mu/([a]-[1]), the denominator's rigid function vanishes only at the trivial character, giving at most a simple pole there.
acceptance: Recover the Kubota-Leopoldt pseudo-measure as a rigid function with a simple pole at the trivial character
Check the p=2 case separately with the {+-1} x (1+4Z_2) chart, verifying the number of components is 2 and not p-1
Verify the multiplicative convolution/pointwise product compatibility on Dirac measures

sources.excerpt: Summarising, W(C_p) = disjoint union over nu in (mu_{p-1})^vee of U_nu, where: nu ranges over the p-1 different characters of mu_{p-1}; U_nu is the subset of characters chi of Z_p^x with chi restricted to mu_{p-1} equal to nu; each U_nu may be identified with B(0,1).
sources.match: The explicit chart decomposition the stage requires, with the p-odd hypothesis visible in the count p-1.

sources.excerpt: a theorem of Amice says that giving a measure mu on Z_p^x is equivalent to giving a bounded rigid analytic function F_mu on W
sources.match: Identifies the comparison theorem the stage needs; RJW gives no proof and no precise citation here, so the proof is an unresolved import (see gaps).

sources.excerpt: So pseudo-measures can be seen as rigid analytic functions on the weight space that possibly have a simple pole at the trivial character.
sources.match: Ties stage L3's pseudo-measures to the rigid picture the stage asks for.

nodes.title: M(G,O_L) is the inverse limit of the finite group algebras O_L[G/H]
nodes.statement: For G a profinite abelian group there is a natural isomorphism of O_L-modules M(G,O_L) -> inverse limit over open subgroups H of O_L[G/H], sending a measure mu (viewed as a finitely additive function on compact opens) to the compatible system lambda_H = sum over cosets aH of mu(aH)[a]. The target is by definition the Iwasawa algebra Lambda(G) = profinite completion of O_L[G].
hypotheses: G profinite abelian; H runs over the open subgroups, which are also compact and of finite index
The isomorphism is at the level of O_L-modules first; it becomes an isomorphism of O_L-algebras once convolution is put on the source (see the convolution node)
Only the integral coefficients O_L are claimed: the analogous statement for L-coefficients is FALSE, since the inverse limit of L[G/H] is strictly larger than M(G,L) = Lambda(G)[1/p]
proofSteps: Restrict to locally constant functions: M(G,O_L) is isomorphic to M^{lc}(G,O_L) = Hom_cts(C^{lc}(G,O_L),O_L) by the density node.
Every locally constant function factors through some finite quotient G/H, so C^{lc}(G,O_L) is the direct limit over H of C(G/H,O_L).
Duals turn the direct limit into an inverse limit: M(G,O_L) is the inverse limit over H of M(G/H,O_L).
For finite abelian G/H, the map [g] -> delta_g identifies O_L[G/H] with M(G/H,O_L) (RJW Prop. 3.15).

The explicit maps are lambda_H = sum_{[a] in G/H} mu(aH)[a] and, backwards, mu(aH) = c_a where lambda_H = sum c_a [a]; compatibility of the lambda_H under projection is exactly finite additivity of mu.
acceptance: Recover the identification of the Dirac measure delta_a on Z_p with the element [a] = ([a+p^n Z_p])_n of the inverse limit
Check the warning: the inverse limit of L[G/H] is not M(G,L); exhibit an element of the former that is unbounded
Check functoriality in G along a surjection of profinite groups, and the augmentation to O_L

sources.locator: Sec. 3.3, Prop. 3.16 and its proof, printed p. 16
sources.excerpt: Proposition 3.16. - We have an natural isomorphism M(G,O_L) = inverse limit over H of O_L[G/H], where the limit is over all open subgroups of G.
sources.match: The stage's central identification; the proof read in the source is the four-step dualisation argument recorded above.

sources.locator: Sec. 3.3, proof of Prop. 3.16, printed p. 16

nodes.title: Convolution and the algebra structure on measures
nodes.statement: For mu, lambda in M(G,O_L) with G profinite abelian, the convolution mu * lambda is defined by integrating phi(x+y) first in y against lambda and then in x against mu. This makes M(G,O_L) an O_L-algebra and the isomorphism M(G,O_L) -> Lambda(G) of the previous node an isomorphism of O_L-algebras; Dirac measures multiply by delta_g * delta_h = delta_{gh}, matching [g][h] = [gh].
hypotheses: G profinite; the written formula uses additive notation and hence commutativity is implicit in RJW's presentation. For a nonabelian G the iterated integral still defines a product but the order of integration matters and the two orders give opposite algebras

Well-definedness needs the interchange of the two integrals, which is proved first for locally constant phi (where both sides are finite sums) and then extended by uniform approximation, using boundedness of both measures
The convolution on measures on Z_p^x uses the multiplicative group law, and is a different operation from the additive convolution on Z_p
proofSteps: Define the pairing on locally constant phi, where both integrals are finite sums over cosets, so the interchange is a finite rearrangement.
Extend to continuous phi by uniform approximation, using that integral measures are bounded by 1 on C(G,O_L), so the approximation is uniform in the second variable.
Check bilinearity and associativity on Dirac measures and extend by density of the span of Dirac measures (Colmez Sec. II.4.1).
Transport to the inverse limit: at each finite level the product is the group-algebra product of O_L[G/H].
acceptance: Verify delta_a * delta_b = delta_{a+b} on Z_p and that the Amice transform sends this to (1+T)^a (1+T)^b = (1+T)^{a+b}

One checks that this does give an algebra structure and that the isomorphism above is an isomorphism of O_L-algebras.

nodes.title: Lambda(Z_p^x) as a non-subalgebra of Lambda(Z_p) and the psi-criterion
nodes.statement: The map iota : Lambda(Z_p^x) -> Lambda(Z_p), defined by integrating the restriction of phi to Z_p^x, is an injective O_L-module map with left inverse Res_{Z_p^x}. Its image is exactly {mu in Lambda(Z_p) : psi(mu) = 0}. It is not a ring homomorphism for the two convolutions.
hypotheses: The operator psi is the one defined on measures by integrating phi(p^{-1}x) over pZ_p; see stage L2
Injectivity uses Res_{Z_p^x} composed with iota being the identity
The identification of the image uses Res_{Z_p^x} = 1 - phi psi and the injectivity of phi
proofSteps: Res_{Z_p^x}(mu) = (1 - phi psi)(mu) from the identities psi phi = id and phi psi = Res_{pZ_p}.
mu is supported on Z_p^x iff Res_{Z_p^x}(mu) = mu iff phi psi (A_mu) = 0 iff psi(A_mu) = 0, since phi is injective on O_L[[T]].
The failure to be a ring map is witnessed by the two different convolution formulas (additive versus multiplicative).

nodes.title: Mahler's theorem: the binomial polynomials are an orthonormal basis of C(Z_p,L)
nodes.statement: Every continuous phi : Z_p -> L has a unique expansion phi(x) = sum_{n>=0} a_n(phi) binom(x,n) with a_n(phi) in L tending to 0, and v_C(phi) = inf_n v_p(a_n(phi)); equivalently phi -> (a_n(phi))_n is an isometry of C(Z_p,L) onto c_0(N,L). The coefficients are the discrete derivatives at 0: a_n(phi) = phi^{[n]}(0), where phi^{[k+1]}(x) = phi^{[k]}(x+1) - phi^{[k]}(x).
hypotheses: L is a complete subfield of C_p; v_p(p)=1
binom(x,n) is continuous Z_p -> Z_p of valuation exactly 0 (Colmez Prop. I.2.1), proved by integrality on n+N and density of n+N in Z_p
Uniform continuity of phi on the compact Z_p is the key input for the surjectivity half (Colmez Lemma I.2.5)
proofSteps: Prop. I.2.1: v_p(binom(x,n)) >= 0 for all x in Z_p since binom(n+k,n) is an integer for k in N and n+N is dense in Z_p; and binom(n,n)=1 gives valuation exactly 0.
The map phi -> a(phi) is continuous into ell-infinity(N,L) with v_{ell-infinity}(a(phi)) >= v_C(phi), directly from the formula for a_n(phi) as an alternating sum of values of phi.
The subspace B of phi with a(phi) in c_0 is closed, since c_0 is closed in ell-infinity.
For a in c_0, the series sum a_n binom(x,n) converges normally in C(Z_p,L) with v_C(phi_a) >= v_{c_0}(a), and Lemma I.2.2 (a_k(P_n) = delta_{kn} for the binomial polynomials) gives a(phi_a) = a.
phi -> a(phi) is injective because a(phi)=0 forces phi(k)=0 for all k in N and N is dense in Z_p; hence phi in B implies phi = phi_{a(phi)}.
Lemma I.2.5: by uniform continuity there is k with v_C(phi^{[p^k]}) >= v_C(phi)+1; iterating shows a_n(phi) -> 0, i.e. B = C(Z_p,L).
acceptance: Check the expansion for phi(x) = x^k and recover the Stirling-type integral combinations
Check the isometry claim numerically on a function with a single nonzero Mahler coefficient

nodes.title: The Mahler-Amice transform M(Z_p,O_L) -> O_L[[T]] is an O_L-algebra isomorphism
nodes.statement: The assignment A_mu(T) = integral over Z_p of (1+T)^x against mu = sum_{n>=0} (integral of binom(x,n) against mu) T^n defines an isomorphism of O_L-algebras M(Z_p,O_L) -> O_L[[T]], compatible with the isomorphism M(Z_p,O_L) -> Lambda(Z_p) of L1 and the isomorphism Lambda(Z_p) -> O_L[[T]] determined by [1] -> 1+T. It sends the Dirac measure delta_a to (1+T)^a. Inverting p gives M(Z_p,L) = O_L[[T]][1/p].
hypotheses: The coefficients lie in O_L exactly because the binomial functions have valuation 0 and mu is an integral measure
Surjectivity uses Mahler's theorem: for arbitrary c_n in O_L, the formula (integral of phi) = sum_n a_n(phi) c_n converges since a_n(phi) -> 0 and the c_n are bounded
The algebra statement is for the ADDITIVE convolution on Z_p; the same formula on Z_p^x does not give a ring map
Only bounded coefficient sequences occur; unbounded ones give distributions, not measures (stage L2's boundary with LocallyAnalyticDistributions)
proofSteps: Injectivity: by Mahler, a measure is determined by its values on the orthonormal basis binom(x,n), i.e. by the coefficients of A_mu.

Surjectivity: given g = sum c_n T^n in O_L[[T]], define the integral of phi = sum a_n(phi) binom(x,n) against mu_g as sum a_n(phi) c_n; convergence holds because a_n(phi) -> 0, and boundedness of (c_n) gives integrality.
Compatibility with the Iwasawa algebra: both composites send delta_a to (1+T)^a, and the span of the Dirac measures is dense, so the triangle (3.4) commutes by continuity.
Multiplicativity then follows from the group-algebra structure of Lambda(Z_p) (previous node) transported along [1] -> 1+T.

nodes.title: Multiplication of a measure by x, by z^x and by a continuous function
nodes.statement: For mu in Lambda(Z_p): (i) A_{x mu} = partial A_mu, where partial = (1+T) d/dT, and hence the integral of x^k against mu equals (partial^k A_mu)(0); (ii) for z in O_L with v_p(z-1) > 0, A_{z^x mu}(T) = A_mu((1+T)^z - 1); (iii) more generally, for g continuous the measure g mu is defined by integrating f g against mu.
hypotheses: In (ii) the hypothesis v_p(z-1) > 0 (equivalently |z-1| < 1) is what makes x -> (1+w)^x = z^x locally analytic and the substitution convergent; Colmez Lemma II.2.1 supplies exactly this
In (i) the identity used is x binom(x,n) = (n+1) binom(x,n+1) + n binom(x,n)
(iii) requires g continuous for measures; for distributions of order r one needs g of class C^r
proofSteps: (i) Compute x binom(x,n) = ((x-n)+n) binom(x,n) = (n+1) binom(x,n+1) + n binom(x,n); summing against T^n gives exactly (1+T) d/dT applied to A_mu.

(ii) By Colmez Lemma II.2.1, for v_p(w) > 0 the integral of (1+w)^x against a continuous distribution lambda is A_lambda(w); applying this to lambda = z^x mu and to mu gives A_{z^x mu}(y-1) = A_mu(yz-1) for all y in B(0,0+), whence the stated substitution formula.
(iii) is the definition; boundedness of g keeps g mu integral when g takes values in O_L.

nodes.title: Restriction of a measure to a residue class and to the units
nodes.statement: For X a compact open subset of Z_p the restriction Res_X(mu) is defined by integrating f 1_X against mu. For X = b + p^n Z_p one has A_{Res_{b+p^n Z_p}(mu)}(T) = p^{-n} sum over the p^n-th roots of unity eta of eta^{-b} A_mu((1+T) eta - 1); in particular A_{Res_{Z_p^x}(mu)}(T) = A_mu(T) - p^{-1} sum over p-th roots of unity xi of A_mu((1+T) xi - 1).
hypotheses: The formula is obtained from the expansion 1_{b+p^n Z_p}(x) = p^{-n} sum_{eta in mu_{p^n}} eta^{x-b}, which requires mu_{p^n} to be available in the coefficient field: one works over L(mu_{p^n}) and descends, the result being independent of the choice because the sum is Galois-stable
The substitution A_mu((1+T)eta - 1) is legitimate by the multiplication-by-z^x lemma, since v_p(eta - 1) > 0 for eta a p-power root of unity

1/p^n appears, so the formula is a priori only an identity in L(mu_{p^n})[[T]]; integrality of the restriction is a separate statement coming from the measure-theoretic definition, not from the formula
proofSteps: Define Res_X(mu) by f -> integral of f 1_X against mu; this is again a measure, and it is integral if mu is.
Expand the characteristic function of b + p^n Z_p in p^n-th roots of unity.
Apply the multiplication-by-z^x rule to each term eta^x, with z = eta and v_p(eta - 1) > 0.
For arbitrary compact open X, write X or its complement as a finite disjoint union of sets b + p^n Z_p and add the formulas.

nodes.title: The operators sigma_a, phi and psi on measures and power series
nodes.statement: For a in Z_p^x define sigma_a(mu) by integrating f(ax); then A_{sigma_a(mu)}(T) = A_mu((1+T)^a - 1). Define phi by integrating f(px), so that A_{phi(mu)}(T) = A_mu((1+T)^p - 1), and psi by the rule that the integral of f against psi(mu) over Z_p equals the integral of f(p^{-1}x) against mu over pZ_p. Then psi phi = id, phi psi = Res_{pZ_p}, hence Res_{Z_p^x} = 1 - phi psi; on power series phi psi (F)(T) = p^{-1} sum over p-th roots of unity xi of F((1+T)xi - 1), and this characterizes psi since phi is injective.

phi is injective on O_L[[T]], which is what allows psi to be recovered from phi psi

Compute the integral of f against phi psi (mu) = the integral of f(px) against psi(mu) over pZ_p = the integral of f against Res_{pZ_p}(mu).
Subtract to obtain Res_{Z_p^x} = 1 - phi psi.
Combine with the roots-of-unity restriction formula to get the displayed identity for phi psi on power series, and use injectivity of phi to define psi.

nodes.title: Matching the strong and weak topologies with the p-adic and (p,T)-adic topologies
nodes.statement: Under the Amice isomorphism M(Z_p,O_L) -> O_L[[T]], the strong (operator-norm) topology on measures corresponds to the p-adic topology on O_L[[T]], which is uniform convergence of the power series coefficients; the weak topology corresponds to the (p,T)-adic topology, which is coefficientwise convergence. The sequence 1, T, T^2, ... converges to 0 in the weak/(p,T)-adic topology but not in the strong/p-adic topology.

'Uniform convergence of coefficients' means convergence in ell-infinity of the coefficient sequences, which is why the strong topology sees 1, T, T^2, ... as a non-convergent sequence

Identify pointwise convergence on the Mahler basis with coefficientwise convergence, i.e. the (p,T)-adic topology.

nodes.title: Pseudo-measures and integration of nontrivial characters
nodes.statement: Let G be profinite abelian and Q(G) the total ring of fractions of Lambda(G). A pseudo-measure is lambda in Q(G) with ([g]-[1]) lambda in Lambda(G) for every g in G. For a nontrivial continuous character chi : G -> C_p^x, the integral of chi against lambda is defined as (chi(g)-1)^{-1} times the integral of chi against ([g]-[1]) lambda for any g with chi(g) not equal to 1, and this is independent of g.
hypotheses: chi must be nontrivial, and g must be chosen with chi(g) not equal to 1; such a g exists precisely because chi is nontrivial
The definition uses that integration of chi is a ring homomorphism Lambda(G) -> C_p for the convolution product, which in turn uses that chi is a character and G is abelian

It does NOT define a homomorphism on all of Q(G): the induced map is defined only on the localization of Lambda(G) at the multiplicative set of elements with nonvanishing chi-integral. RJW Remark 3.35 asserts a unique homomorphism Q(G) -> C_p; that is too strong as stated, because a denominator can have zero chi-integral. Formula (3.11) itself is unaffected, since the denominators [g]-[1] used there are chosen with chi(g) - 1 nonzero
proofSteps: Check that mu -> integral of chi against mu is a ring homomorphism Lambda(G) -> C_p: this is exactly the convolution formula applied to the multiplicative function chi.

Independence of g: multiply out (chi(h)-1) times the integral of chi against ([g]-[1])lambda and (chi(g)-1) times the integral of chi against ([h]-[1])lambda; both equal the integral of chi against ([g]-1)([h]-1)lambda, using commutativity of the convolution.
Record the boundary: the extension of the homomorphism from Lambda(G) to Q(G) is only defined after inverting elements with nonzero chi-integral.
acceptance: Evaluate the Kubota-Leopoldt pseudo-measure at a nontrivial character and check the interpolation formula
Exhibit an element of Q(Z_p^x) at which the naive extension of the character homomorphism is undefined (a nonzero mu with zero chi-integral used as a denominator)

nodes.title: A pseudo-measure on Z_p^x is determined by its positive moments
nodes.statement: (i) If mu in Lambda(Z_p^x) has vanishing integral of x^k for all k > 0 then mu = 0. (ii) If mu in Lambda(Z_p^x) has nonzero integral of x^k for all k > 0 then mu is not a zero divisor in Lambda(Z_p^x). (iii) Statement (i) holds more generally for a pseudo-measure mu.
hypotheses: mu is a measure on Z_p^x (equivalently a measure on Z_p killed by psi)

In (iii) the argument needs an integer a not equal to 1 and prime to p, so that [a]-[1] is a nonzerodivisor by part (ii); for p = 2 such an a exists (e.g. a = 3) but the auxiliary factor must be checked to satisfy part (ii)'s hypothesis
The convolution used in (ii) is the multiplicative one on Z_p^x
proofSteps: (i) The vanishing forces A_mu(T) to be constant, since every nonconstant binomial polynomial is a linear combination of strictly positive powers of x. As mu is supported on the units, psi(A_mu) = 0; but psi is the identity on constants, so A_mu = 0.

(ii) If mu convolved with lambda vanishes then the multiplicativity of moments under multiplicative convolution gives (integral of x^k against mu)(integral of x^k against lambda) = 0 for all k > 0, so lambda has all positive moments zero, and part (i) gives lambda = 0.

(iii) Put lambda = ([a]-[1])mu, a measure by definition of pseudo-measure; its k-th moment is (a^k - 1) times that of mu, hence zero, so lambda = 0 by (i). Since [a]-[1] satisfies the hypothesis of (ii) it is a nonzerodivisor, forcing mu = 0.

nodes.title: Weierstrass division and the finite free quotient Lambda/(distinguished polynomial)
nodes.statement: Let P(T) in O_L[T] be distinguished of degree d, i.e. P = a_0 + ... + a_{d-1}T^{d-1} + T^d with all a_i in the maximal ideal. Then every f in O_L[[T]] can be written uniquely as f = qP + r with q in O_L[[T]] and r a polynomial of degree at most d-1; consequently Lambda/(P) is a free O_L-module of rank d. In particular, for phi_n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} - 1, which is distinguished of degree p^n, Lambda/phi_n(T) is identified with the polynomials of degree at most p^n - 1.
hypotheses: P must be distinguished: its non-leading coefficients lie in the maximal ideal of O_L. For phi_n this holds because all binomial coefficients binom(p^n,k) with 1 <= k < p^n are divisible by p
The coefficient ring must be a complete DVR (or more generally the setting of [BGR84, Sec. 5.2.1]); uniqueness needs completeness
RJW uses the version over Z_p; the O_L version requires the same statement with the uniformizer in place of p

Conclude Lambda/phi_n(T) is isomorphic as an O_L-module to {r in O_L[T] : deg r <= p^n - 1}, hence O_L-free of rank p^n and in particular infinite.

nodes.title: Structure theory of finitely generated Lambda-modules and the characteristic ideal
nodes.statement: Pseudo-isomorphism M ~ M' means the existence of a map with finite kernel and cokernel. Every finitely generated Lambda-module M satisfies M ~ Lambda^r + sum_i Lambda/(p^{n_i}) + sum_j Lambda/(f_j(T)^{m_j}) with f_j irreducible distinguished. For M finitely generated torsion (so r = 0) the characteristic ideal is Ch_Lambda(M) = (p^n prod_j f_j^{m_j}) with n = sum_i n_i. For Gamma = H x Gamma' with H finite of order prime to p and Gamma' isomorphic to Z_p, the idempotents e_omega decompose M into isotypic pieces and Ch_{Lambda(Gamma)}(M) is defined componentwise; the characteristic ideal is multiplicative in short exact sequences.
hypotheses: Pseudo-isomorphism is NOT an equivalence relation on arbitrary finitely generated Lambda-modules; it is one on finitely generated TORSION modules. RJW records this explicitly, citing [Was97, Warning, Sec. 13.2]

The isotypic decomposition requires |H| prime to p; the idempotents e_omega = |H|^{-1} sum_a omega^{-1}(a)[a] require dividing by |H| and possibly enlarging L to contain the values of omega. For p-torsion in H the decomposition is unavailable

The vertical elementary divisors are written as powers of p in RJW because Lambda is taken over O_L with the p-adic filtration; over a general O_L the correct invariants are powers of a uniformizer, and mu must be measured with v_uniformizer
Multiplicativity (Lemma 13.6) and the isotypic decomposition (Lemma 13.4) are quoted from [CS06, A.1] without proof in RJW
proofSteps: Structure theorem: RJW Theorem 13.1 is quoted from [Was97, Thm. 13.12]; no proof is given in RJW. The statement fixes the shape of the elementary module A.
Definition 13.3 defines the characteristic ideal from the elementary divisors of A; the intrinsic description via lengths at height-one primes is not given in RJW and remains to be supplied.
Lemma 13.4 gives M = sum over omega of M^{(omega)} with each factor finitely generated torsion over Lambda, quoted from [CS06, A.1].

Definition 13.5 then sets Ch_{Lambda(Gamma)}(M) as the sum of the componentwise characteristic ideals, and Lemma 13.6 records multiplicativity in exact sequences, also quoted from [CS06, A.1 Prop. 1].

nodes.statement: Let A = Lambda^r + sum_i Lambda/(p^{m_i}) + sum_j Lambda/(f_j(T)^{k_j}) with f_j distinguished, m = sum_i m_i and l = sum_j k_j deg(f_j). If A/phi_n(T)A is finite for all n then r = 0, and there are constants n_0 and c with |A/phi_n(T)| = p^{m p^n + l n + c} for all n >= n_0.
